states.name: Alaska
states.agency: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Office of Boating Safety

rule.textEn: Alaska has no mandatory boater education. An optional Alaska Boater Education card exists and is useful when boating in states that require one.
rule.textEs: Alaska no exige educación náutica. Existe una tarjeta opcional de educación náutica de Alaska, útil para navegar en estados que sí la exigen.

card.feeNote: The state also offers a free course, Alaska Water Wise.

sources.publisher: Alaska Department of Natural Resources
sources.quote: Alaska is one of the few states that do not require boating education.

sources.publisher: Alaska Department of Natural Resources
sources.quote: Our free Alaska Water Wise course was designed by us for Alaskan boaters.

states.name: Alabama
states.agency: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (Marine Patrol Division)

rule.textEn: Every operator of a motorized vessel, including personal watercraft, needs an Alabama vessel operator license (a "V" class on the driver license) or, for nonresidents, a home-state certificate.
rule.textEs: Todo operador de una embarcación con motor, incluidas las motos acuáticas, necesita la licencia de operador de embarcaciones de Alabama (clase "V" en la licencia de conducir) o, si no reside allí, un certificado de su estado.

minAge.note: Licence possible from 12; ages 12-13 hold a learner license and need a licensed person 21+ on board.

exemptions: Born before April 28, 1954: no written exam (the license is still needed).
Holders of a valid US Coast Guard motorboat operator license are exempt from the exam.

card.feeNote: One-time $5 application fee plus a $36.25 license issuance fee; approved online courses are sold separately by private providers.

states.nonResident: Since Oct. 1, 2024 a visitor needs a boater certificate from the home state or country, or an Alabama nonresident certification.

sources.publisher: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency
sources.quote: A one-time application fee of $5.00 cash will be charged. There will be a $36.25 issuance fee for the license.

sources.publisher: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency
sources.quote: Must be 12 years old or older to be eligible for a vessel operator's license but cannot operate alone until the age of 14.

sources.publisher: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency
sources.quote: Effective October 1, 2024: Nonresidents may operate a vessel upon the waters of this state only after obtaining a valid boater safety certification or vessel operator's certification issued in his or her home state or country

sources.publisher: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency
sources.quote: Any boat operator who was born prior to April 28, 1954

sources.publisher: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency
sources.quote: Under age 14, Vessel Learner License only. Must be accompanied by a Vessel Licensed driver that is 21 years old or older.

states.name: Arkansas
states.agency: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission

rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1986 needs an approved boating education course to run a motorboat or a sailboat.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1986 o después necesita un curso de navegación aprobado para manejar una lancha con motor o un velero.

minAge.note: Motorboat of 10 hp or more: 12+, or younger with a supervisor 18+. PWC: 16+, ages 12-15 with a supervisor 18+, under 12 with a supervisor 21+.

sources.publisher: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission
sources.quote: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1986, and of legal age to operate a motorboat or sailboat, must have successfully completed an approved AGFC Boating Education Course to operate a motorboat or sailboat on Arkansas water.

sources.publisher: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission
sources.quote: To operate a personal watercraft, a person must be 16 or older, be 12 to 15 years old and be under the direct supervision of a person at least 18 years old, or be under 12 and be under the direct supervision of a person at least 21 years old.

states.name: Arizona
states.agency: Arizona Game and Fish Department

rule.textEn: Arizona has no general boater education requirement; a course is only mandatory when a court orders it after a boating citation. The state offers free courses.
rule.textEs: Arizona no tiene un requisito general de educación náutica; el curso solo es obligatorio cuando un juez lo ordena tras una multa. El estado ofrece cursos gratuitos.

card.feeNote: AZGFD offers a free home study packet and classes.

sources.publisher: Arizona Game and Fish Department (archived copy of 2026-04-07; live page answers 403 to scripts)
sources.quote: Need to complete a boating safety education course because of a boating ticket? Choose an option below to meet the court’s requirements.

sources.publisher: Arizona Game and Fish Department
sources.quote: Fill out the Home Study Packet Request Form or email [email protected] to get your free home study packet.

uncertain: required (no explicit official sentence saying no requirement; AZGFD only describes court-ordered and voluntary courses)

states.name: California
states.agency: California State Parks, Division of Boating and Waterways

rule.phaseIn: Phased in by age from 2018; since Jan. 1, 2025 it covers all ages.
rule.textEn: Since Jan. 1, 2025 every operator of a motorized recreational vessel, whatever the age, must carry a California Boater Card.
rule.textEs: Desde el 1 de enero de 2025 todo operador de una embarcación recreativa con motor, de cualquier edad, debe llevar la California Boater Card.

minAge.note: Under 16 may not run a motor over 15 hp (sailboats up to 30 ft excepted); ages 12-15 may with an adult 18+ on board.

exemptions: Operating a rental vessel.
Under the direct supervision of an adult 18+ who holds a card.
Out-of-state visitor boating fewer than 60 days who meets home-state rules (90 days for a foreign visitor).
Holders of a current commercial fishing license or a US Coast Guard marine operator license.

card.feeNote: Lifetime card issued by the Division of Boating and Waterways; courses are separate (free and paid courses exist).

states.nonResident: A visitor boating in California for fewer than 60 days who meets the home-state requirement does not need the card (90 days for foreign visitors).
states.rental: Renters are exempt from the card.

sources.publisher: California State Parks, Division of Boating and Waterways
sources.quote: The lifetime card fee will be $10. The lost card replacement fee will be $5.

sources.publisher: California State Parks, Division of Boating and Waterways
sources.quote: January 1, 2025 All persons regardless of age

sources.publisher: California State Parks, Division of Boating and Waterways
sources.quote: NO person under 16 years of age may operate a boat with a motor of more than 15 horsepower

sources.publisher: California State Parks, Division of Boating and Waterways
sources.quote: A person operating a rental vessel.

states.name: Colorado
states.agency: Colorado Parks and Wildlife

rule.textEn: Motorboats and PWC: operators must be 18, except that 14- to 17-year-olds may operate after passing a state-approved boating safety course.
rule.textEs: Lanchas con motor y motos acuáticas: hay que tener 18 años, salvo los de 14 a 17 años que aprueben un curso de seguridad náutica aprobado por el estado.

minAge.note: Under 14 may not operate a motorboat or PWC; 14-17 only with the course; 18+ no course required.

sources.publisher: Colorado Parks and Wildlife
sources.quote: In Colorado, anyone operating a motorboat - including personal watercraft such as Jet Skis - must be at least 18 years old.

sources.publisher: Colorado Parks and Wildlife
sources.quote: Individuals aged 14–17 who wish to operate a motorized vessel are required to complete and pass a state-approved boating safety course. Courses may be taken in person, virtually, or fully online through an approved provider.

states.name: Connecticut
states.agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)

rule.textEn: Connecticut residents (and owners of property or boats kept in the state, or anyone boating more than 60 days a year) need a Safe Boating Certificate for any registered boat, and a Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation for a PWC.
rule.textEs: Los residentes de Connecticut (y quienes tienen propiedad o barco en el estado, o navegan más de 60 días al año) necesitan el Safe Boating Certificate para cualquier barco registrado, y el Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation para una moto acuática.

minAge.note: Under 16 may run a boat other than a PWC uncertified only under direct supervision of a person 18+ certified for at least two years; PWC under 16 only with such a person on board.

exemptions: US Coast Guard master, mate or pilot license (not valid for PWC or towed sports).

card.nameEn: Safe Boating Certificate (SBC) / Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation (CPWO)
card.feeNote: One-time $50 certificate fee; the DEEP equivalency exam costs $75; a 3-month temporary certificate costs $50; duplicates can be printed free.

states.nonResident: Visitors need the certificate if their boat must display a Connecticut decal or they boat more than 60 days a year in the state.

sources.publisher: Connecticut DEEP
sources.quote: Currently there is a onetime fee of $50 for a boating certificate.

sources.publisher: Connecticut DEEP
sources.quote: The examination fee is $75.00. Testing is by appointment only.

sources.publisher: Connecticut DEEP
sources.quote: No, asynchronous courses are not approved.

sources.publisher: Connecticut DEEP
sources.quote: If you are a Connecticut resident operating a registered boat of any kind you must possess a Safe Boating Certificate or Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation.

sources.publisher: Connecticut DEEP
sources.quote: By law, any person under the age of 16 may operate a vessel (other than a personal watercraft) without being certified if under the direct supervision of a person 18 or older, who has had their Safe Boating Certificate (SBC) or Certificate of Personal Watercraft Operation (CPWO) for at least two years.

sources.publisher: Connecticut DEEP
sources.quote: You operate your vessel on CT waters for more than 60 days in a calendar year

uncertain: card.replacementFee (duplicates printed free online, per DEEP search result, not re-read)

states.name: District of Columbia
states.agency: Metropolitan Police Department, Harbor Patrol Unit

rule.textEn: Anyone operating a vessel on District of Columbia waterways must hold a Boating Safety Certificate.
rule.textEs: Toda persona que maneje una embarcación en las aguas del Distrito de Columbia debe tener un Boating Safety Certificate.

card.feeNote: MPD Harbor Patrol runs a free one-day, 8-hour course (pre-registration by phone).

sources.publisher: Metropolitan Police Department
sources.quote: Anyone operating a vessel on District of Columbia waterways is required to have a Boating Safety Certificate.

sources.publisher: Metropolitan Police Department
sources.quote: The training is free; photo ID is required.

states.name: Delaware
states.agency: Delaware DNREC, Division of Fish and Wildlife

rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1978 must pass a boating safety course before running any motorized boat, PWC included.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1978 o después debe aprobar un curso de seguridad náutica antes de manejar cualquier embarcación con motor, incluidas las motos acuáticas.

minAge.note: PWC from 14 with the course and an adult on board at 14-15; alone from 16 with the certificate.

sources.publisher: Delaware DNREC
sources.quote: Persons born on or after January 1, 1978 must successfully complete a boating safety course before operating a motorized boat, including personal watercraft, on Delaware waters.

sources.publisher: Delaware DNREC
sources.quote: Personal watercraft operators who are 14 and 15 years old are required to have an adult on board. Those who are 16 years of age, who hold a boating safety education certificate, can operate without adult supervision.

sources.publisher: Delaware DNREC
sources.quote: Several online courses also meet the requirement.

states.name: Florida
states.agency: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC)

rule.hpNote: 10 hp or more
rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1988 needs an approved course and an FWC Boating Safety Education ID Card to run a motorboat of 10 hp or more.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1988 o después necesita un curso aprobado y la tarjeta Boating Safety Education ID de la FWC para manejar una lancha de 10 hp o más.

exemptions: Accompanied on board by a card holder 18+ (or an exempt person) responsible for the boat.
Nonresident with proof of a NASBLA-approved course and a photo ID.
A course completion certificate plus photo ID works for 90 days.
A 90-day temporary certificate exam is sold by FWC-authorized vendors (Florida only).

card.feeNote: Approved course prices are set by providers; FWC lists free and paid options.

states.nonResident: Visitors born on or after Jan. 1, 1988 need proof of a NASBLA-approved course (or a temporary certificate) and photo ID.
states.rental: Visitors can rent with a 90-day temporary certificate after an exam at an FWC-authorized vendor.

sources.publisher: Florida FWC (archived copy of 2026-06-06; live page blocked by Cloudflare for scripts)
sources.quote: To operate a motorboat of ten (10) horsepower or greater requires anyone who was born on or after Jan. 1, 1988 , to successfully complete an approved boating safety course and obtain a Boating Safety Education Identification Card issued by the FWC.

sources.publisher: Florida FWC
sources.quote: A nonresident who has in his or her possession proof that he or she has completed a NASBLA-approved boater safety course or equivalency examination from another state AND a photographic I.D.

sources.publisher: Florida FWC
sources.quote: The temporary certificate cannot be submitted for issuance of a Boating Safety Education ID card that is valid for life.

states.name: Georgia
states.agency: Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Law Enforcement Division

rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1998 must have passed a DNR-approved boater education course to run any motorized vessel.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1998 o después debe haber aprobado un curso de educación náutica aprobado por el DNR para manejar cualquier embarcación con motor.

minAge.note: Under 12: only boats under 16 ft, non-motorized or 30 hp or less, with a competent adult. 12-15: boats under 16 ft incl. PWC with the course or a competent adult; nothing over 16 ft.

exemptions: US Coast Guard master license.
Operating on a private lake or pond.
Nonresident with proof of a NASBLA-approved course or equivalency exam from another state.
states.nonResident: Visitors with proof of a NASBLA-approved course from another state are exempt.

sources.publisher: Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Division
sources.quote: As of July 1, 2014, all persons born on or after January 1, 1998 that operate any motorized vessel on the waters of the state must have completed a boat education course approved by the department prior to such operation.

sources.publisher: Georgia DNR
sources.quote: a non-resident who has in his or her possession proof that he or she has completed a NASBLA approved boater education course or equivalency examination from another state.

sources.publisher: Georgia DNR Law Enforcement Division
sources.quote: May legally operate a vessel under 16 feet in length which is either non-motorized or powered by a motor of 30 horsepower or less only if they are accompanied by a competent adult.

sources.publisher: Georgia Department of Natural Resources
sources.quote: A person is exempt if he or she is: a person licensed by the U.S. Coast Guard as a master of a vessel; a person operating on a private lake or pond;

states.name: Hawaii
states.agency: Hawaii DLNR, Division of Boating and Ocean Recreation (DOBOR)

rule.hpNote: more than 10 hp (sailboats with an auxiliary engine over 10 hp included)
rule.textEn: Anyone running a motorized vessel with more than 10 hp in Hawaii waters needs a NASBLA- and state-approved boating course; PWC (thrill craft) also need a separate thrill craft certification.
rule.textEs: Quien maneje una embarcación con motor de más de 10 hp en aguas de Hawái necesita un curso náutico aprobado por NASBLA y el estado; las motos acuáticas exigen además una certificación propia (thrill craft).

minAge.note: Under 16: needs the certificate and direct supervision by a certified adult 21+.

exemptions: Vessels of 10 hp or less.
Out-of-state visitors on a voyage from elsewhere staying fewer than 60 days.
Rental operators who received a state-approved safety briefing.
Commercial thrill craft customers in state-authorized zones.

card.nameEn: Boating safety course certificate (+ thrill craft operator certification for PWC)

states.nonResident: Visitors arriving on a voyage from elsewhere are exempt for fewer than 60 days.
states.rental: Renters are exempt after a state-approved safety briefing.
states.pwcExtra: PWC need a separate thrill craft operator certification on top of the boating course.

sources.publisher: Hawaii DLNR DOBOR
sources.quote: To operate a recreational motorized vessel powered by an engine over 10 hp in Hawaiʻi, you must have one credentials: (1) a National Association of State Boating Law Administrators (NASBLA) and State-approved basic boating safety course for motorized vessels.

sources.publisher: Hawaii DLNR DOBOR
sources.quote: Under-16 operators: Must have the required certificate and be directly supervised by an adult (21+ years old) who also holds the required certificate.

sources.publisher: Hawaii DLNR DOBOR
sources.quote: Out-of-state visitors on a voyage originating elsewhere, staying in Hawai‘i for less than 60 calendar days .

sources.publisher: Hawaii DLNR DOBOR
sources.quote: Rental vessel operators who have received a State-approved safety briefing .

sources.publisher: Hawaii DLNR DOBOR
sources.quote: Fines: Minimum $50 up to $1,000 per violation.

states.name: Iowa
states.agency: Iowa Department of Natural Resources

rule.hpNote: more than 10 hp
rule.textEn: Ages 12 to 17 need an approved boater education course to run a motorboat over 10 hp or a PWC, unless an experienced person 18+ is on board.
rule.textEs: De 12 a 17 años hace falta un curso de educación náutica aprobado para manejar una lancha de más de 10 hp o una moto acuática, salvo que vaya a bordo una persona experimentada de 18 años o más.

minAge.note: 12-17: course or an experienced person 18+ on board.

exemptions: Accompanied on board by an experienced, responsible person 18+.

card.feeNote: Online providers add a $5 Iowa state fee for the permanent certificate; the BoatUS Foundation course is the only free course approved by Iowa DNR.

sources.publisher: Iowa DNR
sources.quote: Any person 12 - 17 years old, can operate a motorboat over ten horsepower or personal watercraft (PWC) if he or she ... is accompanied on board by a responsible person who is at least 18 years old and experienced in operating the vessel.

sources.publisher: Iowa DNR
sources.quote: The cost is $54.95, plus $5 to Iowa DNR for your permanent ca[rd]

sources.publisher: Iowa DNR
sources.quote: The BoatUS Foundation's Online Boating Safety Course is the only free course approved by the Iowa Department of Natural Resources.

states.name: Idaho
states.agency: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation

rule.textEn: Idaho has no general boater education requirement. Education is only mandatory for PWC renters (given by the rental business) and for operators convicted of BUI or repeat boating violations.
rule.textEs: Idaho no tiene un requisito general de educación náutica. Solo es obligatoria para quien alquila una moto acuática (la imparte el negocio de alquiler) y para quienes son condenados por manejar bajo los efectos del alcohol o por infracciones náuticas repetidas.

minAge.note: No statewide minimum operating age; some counties (e.g. Benewah, Bonner, Kootenai) set local age rules.

card.feeNote: IDPR offers free in-person classes and a free home-study guide and test; approved online vendors may charge.

states.rental: PWC rental businesses must educate every renter who will operate the PWC; the operator carries a verification wallet card.
states.penalty: A course is ordered after a BUI conviction or repeat boating-law violations.

sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Handbook of Idaho Boating Laws and Responsibilities (2021 ed., Wayback Machine copy of 2026-01-25)
sources.quote: Although there is no statewide law specifying a minimum age to operate a vessel, all operators must be competent and are held responsible for knowing the navigation rules.

sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Handbook of Idaho Boating Laws and Responsibilities (2021 ed., Wayback Machine copy of 2026-01-25)
sources.quote: Idaho law requires boater education under these conditions.

sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Handbook of Idaho Boating Laws and Responsibilities (2021 ed., Wayback Machine copy of 2026-01-25)
sources.quote: PWC rental businesses must provide education to each person who will ride and operate the PWC. The operator of the PWC must carry a verification wallet card.

sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Handbook of Idaho Boating Laws and Responsibilities (2021 ed., Wayback Machine copy of 2026-01-25)
sources.quote: boat operators are required to pass a boating course if they are convicted of operating under the influence of drugs or alcohol.

sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Handbook of Idaho Boating Laws and Responsibilities (2021 ed., Wayback Machine copy of 2026-01-25)
sources.quote: Boat operators who are repeat offenders of any boating law or rule also are required to pass a boating course.

sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Boating page (Wayback Machine copy of 2026-10-17)
sources.quote: Home Study Guide . Review materials (in the guide) and take a test (in the same guide), all in the comfort of your own home at your own pace (no cost).

sources.publisher: Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation, Boating page (Wayback Machine copy of 2026-10-17)
sources.quote: Online Education . The following vendors are   approved for the state of Idaho (fees may apply).

states.name: Illinois
states.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources

rule.hpNote: more than 10 hp
rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1998 needs a boating safety certificate to run a motorboat over 10 hp, PWC included.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1998 o después necesita un certificado de seguridad náutica para manejar una lancha de más de 10 hp, incluidas las motos acuáticas.

minAge.note: Under 10: no motorboat. 10-11: over 10 hp only with a parent or designated adult 18+ on board. 12-17: with the certificate or that supervision.

exemptions: Born before Jan. 1, 1998.

card.feeNote: Classroom courses by volunteer instructors are free; online courses cost $34.95 to $59.95 (IDNR figures).

sources.publisher: Illinois DNR
sources.quote: Persons born on or after January 1, 1998, may operate a motorboat with more than 10 horsepower, including personal watercraft, only if they have a valid boating safety certificate accepted by the Illinois Department of Natural Resources ( 625 ILCS 45/5-18 ).

sources.publisher: Illinois DNR
sources.quote: No person under 10 years of age may operate a motorboat, including personal watercraft ( 625 ILCS 45/5-18 ).

sources.publisher: Illinois DNR
sources.quote: The online course fee varies by course ($34.95-$59.95).

states.name: Indiana
states.agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Law Enforcement Division

rule.hpNote: more than 10 hp
rule.textEn: To run a motorboat over 10 hp you need a valid driver license; without one, you must be at least 15, have passed a boater education course and hold a BMV ID card.
rule.textEs: Para manejar una lancha de más de 10 hp hace falta una licencia de conducir vigente; sin ella, hay que tener al menos 15 años, haber aprobado un curso de educación náutica y tener una tarjeta de identificación del BMV.

minAge.note: Without a driver license: 15+ with the course and a BMV ID card.

sources.publisher: State of Indiana
sources.quote: The operator of a motorboat, of more than 10 horsepower must have a valid driver’s license or be at least 15 years old and have passed a Boater Education Course and possess an identification card issued from the Bureau of Motor Vehicles. IC 14-15-11.

states.name: Kansas
states.agency: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks

rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1989 who is under 21 needs a boater safety education certificate to run a motorboat or sailboat, unless supervised by a qualified person over 17.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de enero de 1989 o después y tiene menos de 21 años necesita un certificado de educación náutica para manejar una lancha o un velero, salvo que lo supervise una persona habilitada mayor de 17 años.

exemptions: Age 21 or older.
Under the direct and audible supervision of a person over 17 who holds a certificate or is exempt.
Non-motorized sailboat 16 ft 7 in or shorter during an instructor-led class.

sources.publisher: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes (K.S.A. 32-1139)
sources.quote: No person born on or after January 1, 1989, shall operate on public waters of this state any motorboat or sailboat unless the person possesses a certificate of completion of an approved boater safety education course

sources.publisher: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes (K.S.A. 32-1139)
sources.quote: The requirement in subsection (a)(1), shall not apply to a person 21 years of age or older.

states.name: Kentucky
states.agency: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources

rule.hpNote: more than 10 hp
rule.textEn: Ages 12 through 17 need a safe boating certificate to run a PWC or a motorboat over 10 hp, unless a person 18+ is on board.
rule.textEs: De 12 a 17 años hace falta un certificado de navegación segura para manejar una moto acuática o una lancha de más de 10 hp, salvo que vaya a bordo una persona de 18 años o más.

minAge.note: Under 12 may not run a PWC or a motorboat over 10 hp.

exemptions: A person 18 or older on board.
states.nonResident: Nonresidents aged 12-17 need a Kentucky certificate or an equivalent one from their state or country.

sources.publisher: Kentucky Legislative Research Commission (KRS 235.285)
sources.quote: a person twelve (12) years of age through seventeen (17) years of age shall not operate a personal watercraft or motorboat over ten (10) horsepower on the public waters of the Commonwealth unless the person is in possession of a safe boating certificate or is accompanied, on board, by a person eighteen (18) years of age or older

sources.publisher: Kentucky Legislative Research Commission (KRS 235.285)
sources.quote: A person under twelve (12) years of age shall not operate a personal watercraft or motorboat over ten (10) horsepower

states.name: Louisiana
states.agency: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries (LDWF)

rule.hpNote: more than 10 hp
rule.textEn: Anyone born after Jan. 1, 1984 needs an LDWF-approved boater education course to run a motorboat over 10 hp (or a qualified adult over 18 on board) and always to run a PWC.
rule.textEs: Quien nació después del 1 de enero de 1984 necesita un curso aprobado por LDWF para manejar una lancha de más de 10 hp (o un adulto habilitado mayor de 18 a bordo) y siempre para una moto acuática.

minAge.note: PWC operators must be 16 or older.

exemptions: Accompanied by someone over 18 who completed an approved course (not for PWC).
US Coast Guard licensed captain.

card.feeNote: LDWF classroom course is free; the BoatUS online course is free; a free boater education endorsement can be added to the driver license at renewal.

states.rental: Renters (18+) of boats over 10 hp from a state-approved livery watch a safety video that gives a 48-hour exemption.

sources.publisher: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries
sources.quote: if you were born after January 1, 1984, you must successfully complete an LDWF-approved boater education course to operate a motorboat over 10 horsepower, unless you are accompanied by someone over age 18 who has a successfully completed an LDWF-approved boater education course

sources.publisher: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries
sources.quote: You must also be age 16 or older to operate a personal watercraft.

sources.publisher: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries
sources.quote: LDWF offers a free, in-person boater education course that satisfies boater education requirements.

sources.publisher: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries
sources.quote: After watching this rental boating safety and education video, individuals have a 48-hour exemption to operate a rented vessel from a state-approved livery.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.agency: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau

rule.hpNote: any motorboat (any vessel with machinery propulsion, PWC included)
rule.phaseIn: Hanson-Milone Act: born after Jan. 1, 1989 from April 1, 2026; everyone by April 1, 2028. No penalties before Sept. 1, 2026.
rule.textEn: Under the Hanson-Milone Act, anyone born after Jan. 1, 1989 needs a boater safety certificate to run a motorboat or PWC since April 1, 2026; older operators must have one by April 1, 2028.
rule.textEs: Según la Ley Hanson-Milone, quien nació después del 1 de enero de 1989 necesita un certificado de seguridad náutica para manejar una lancha o moto acuática desde el 1 de abril de 2026; los demás deberán tenerlo a más tardar el 1 de abril de 2028.

minAge.note: PWC only from 16, even with a certificate. The course is open from 12. Someone over 12 without a certificate may operate under direct supervision of a certified person over 18.

exemptions: Direct supervision by a certified person over 18 (operator over 12).
Holders of a valid merchant mariner credential or similar license.
Non-residents with a certificate from another U.S. state or territory or Canada.
Active military, National Guard or Coast Guard members qualified to run motorboats.
New owners within 6 months of buying a numbered or documented boat, with a temporary certificate.
Commercial fishing vessel operators; students in an approved course; approved boating safety programs.
Paddlecraft without a motor; USCG-documented vessels are not motorboats under the Act.

card.feeNote: The state charges no fee for the course or certificate; MEP classes are free, private providers may charge. Replacement via ilostmycard.com.

states.nonResident: Visitors with a certificate from any U.S. state or territory or from Transport Canada are exempt; Massachusetts residents need a Massachusetts certificate (out-of-state ones can be converted).
states.rental: Renters are not exempt; the Environmental Police is studying temporary certificates for low-power rentals.
states.pwcExtra: PWC operators must be 16 or older and hold a certificate.
states.penalty: $50 first offense, $100 for later offenses; no penalties before Sept. 1, 2026.

sources.publisher: Massachusetts Environmental Police, Boat and Recreation Vehicle Safety Bureau

rule.textEn: Wyoming has no mandatory boater education. Operators of a registered motorboat or PWC must be 16, or younger with an adult 18+ aboard.
rule.textEs: Wyoming no exige educación náutica obligatoria. Quien maneje una lancha registrada o una moto acuática debe tener 16 años, o menos si va a bordo un adulto de 18 años o más.

minAge.note: Under 16 may operate a motorboat or PWC only with an adult 18+ physically aboard and responsible. No age limit for non-motorized craft.

card.feeNote: Game and Fish gives a free Boat America home-study packet and exam; the online courses are free to take but charge $29.95 for the exam and card.

states.pwcExtra: Same age rule as motorboats: 16, or younger with an adult 18+ aboard.

sources.publisher: Wyoming Game and Fish Department
sources.quote: Possessing a boating safety certificate card is required by some states - but not in Wyoming - in order to operate motorboats

sources.publisher: Wyoming Game and Fish Department
sources.quote: The Wyoming Game and Fish Department offers a free “Boat America” home study course packet and exam

sources.publisher: Wyoming Game and Fish Department
sources.quote: These courses are free to take but require a $29.95 examination and certificate printing fee.

sources.publisher: Wyoming Game and Fish Department
sources.quote: To legally operate a motorboat, the operator must be at least 16 years old. A person under the age of 16 may operate a motorboat as long as they are accompanied by an adult who is at least 18 years old.

sources.publisher: Wyoming Game and Fish Department, 2023 Wyoming Watercraft Regulation
sources.quote: by a person under sixteen (16) years of age who is not accompanied by an adult. (This includes personal watercraft, i.e., jet skis.)

sources.publisher: Wyoming Game and Fish Department
sources.quote: There is no age restriction to operate a non-motorized watercraft, like a canoe, kayak or raft.
